title: Tscn and Tres files Won't Open After Using the Tres as an @export var my_variable: MyClassName in the Tscn
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6.3 stable, 4.7 stable, and 4.7.1.rc1.

### System information

Godot v4.6.3.stable - Fedora Linux 44 (Workstation Edition) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER (nvidia; 595.80) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-13600K (20 threads) - 31.16 GiB memory

### Issue description

Note:
This will corrupt files inside the attached mrp Godot project. Or at least make them unopenable within Godot.

Adding a script with `@export var my_variable: MyClassNameResource` to a .tscn scene file, and filling it out in the Inspector with a .tres file (that uses the .tscn file) causes involved files to no longer open in Godot.

### Steps to reproduce

- Also see video recording: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bd0a394-76c9-44cd-8e2f-0724d1b996b3

 - open the attached mrp Godot Project
 - note [MyClassNameResource.gd](http://myclassnameresource.gd/) which has this code:
```
extends Resource
class_name MyClassNameResource

@export var item_name: String
@export var damage: int
@export var scene_of_item: PackedScene
@export var ui_art_for_item: Texture2D
```
 - also note sword.tres, which already has its values in the Inspector filled out/assigned
 - open sword_static_body_3d.tscn
 - select its StaticBody3D node
 - attach a new script to it and give it this code:
```
extends StaticBody3D

@export var my_variable: MyClassNameResource
```
 - assign the sword.tres to my_variable in the Inspector
 - Save and quit Godot
 - reopen the project
 - there will be missing dependencies, even though the files are still there
 - trying to fix the dependencies won't work, though
 - and you can no longer open these files in Godot (sword_static_body_3d.tscn and sword.tres) (even if the missing dependencies message doesn't appear if you quit and reopen the project again)
 - You can open the .tres file in a text editor, though, and in there it seems fine

How I Expect it to Behave and Work:
 - I expected it to simply reopen without any missing dependencies or broken files
 - If I'm coding my game incorrectly (am I making a circular reference?), I expect it to give me an error message, instead of breaking files and having missing dependencies when I didn't delete anything.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[mrp-missing-dependencies-class-name-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29611079/mrp-missing-dependencies-class-name-bug.zip)
